title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: a refractory-element pool such as Nb–Mo–Ta–W–V combined with ductility-enhancing elements (Ti, Zr, Hf), and possibly limited Cr (or Si/B) for oxidation control.
recollection.intervention: Guess: a composition-design framework combining simple descriptors (VEC ~4.3–4.8, atomic-size mismatch δ < ~4–5%, enthalpy/Ω criteria) with CALPHAD/DFT or data-driven screening to select BCC-stable RHEAs; experimental validation via vacuum arc melting/casting and homogenization, with tuning of short-range order to suppress brittle intermetallics.
recollection.structure: Guess: predominantly single-phase BCC (A2) solid solution at room temperature with controlled short-range order; optionally minor coherent B2 precipitates suppressed or kept below a small volume fraction; thermally stable BCC up to ~1100–1200 °C.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: stabilization of a ductile BCC solid solution by balancing high-VEC strengtheners (Mo, W, Ta) with low-Peierls, large-size elements (Ti, Zr, Hf) to enable dislocation glide; solid-solution strengthening via lattice distortion and SRO; avoidance of strongly negative pairwise enthalpy combinations to prevent Laves/σ; improved high-T strength via sluggish diffusion and maintained SRO.
recollection.results: Guess: designed alloys achieved room-temperature yield strengths ~1.4–2.0 GPa with tensile elongations ~8–15%; high-temperature yield/creep strength ~250–400 MPa at ~1100–1200 °C; single-phase BCC confirmed by XRD/EBSD with grain sizes tens of microns; hardness ~4.5–6 GPa; some variants with Cr formed protective scales and showed improved oxidation resistance while maintaining BCC stability.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies the Nb–Mo–Ta–V–W element pool, arc melting, and a single-phase BCC outcome, but it misses the actual modulus/VEC screening of 38,326 compositions and the selected Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 composition. Its mechanism loosely invokes Peierls-controlled dislocation glide, but incorrectly centers Ti/Zr/Hf, lattice distortion, SRO, and high-temperature behavior. Reported strengths, ductility, grain size, and high-temperature results are wrong or invented; only the hardness range is roughly near the measured Vickers hardness.
